newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian forces say take last royalist-held town.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian forces say take last royalist-held town.

text.p: Cambodian government forces on Tuesday seized the last town held by loyalists of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, government military officials said.
The town of O'Smach fell at 1:10 p.m. (0610 GMT) and royalist troops were fleeing the area, said Nuo Sam, first deputy governor of the northwest province of Siem Reap.

A senior military official told Reuters the government forces, under the control of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, had captured O'Smach slightly later, at around 2 p.m. (0700 GMT), after a major offensive on Tuesday.
He said Hun Sen's troops had seized seven royalist tanks but had no information on any prisoners or casualties.
There was no confirmation available from the immediate area of the fighting, and a Thai military official on the border said he believed that O'Smach remained in royalist hands.

Ranariddh's ragged army has been battling the government forces since Hun Sen overthrew the prince on July 6. The fighting sent 20,000 civilians fleeing over the border to Thailand late on Monday night.
